title_en:
Oliver Ames Sr. was a prominent American blacksmith and industrialist, best known for founding the Ames Shovel Works in Easton, Massachusetts. His contributions to shovel manufacturing significantly impacted the industry and helped establish a family fortune.

Oliver introduced the first back-strapped shovels in 1817, which improved usability, and his company became known for producing high-quality shovels that were essential for major construction projects like the transcontinental railroad and the Panama Canal. Additionally, after a fire in 1852, Ames rebuilt his factories using fireproof granite, enhancing safety and durability in production.

Oliver Ames Sr. established the Ames Shovel Works, which became a major manufacturer of shovels and other tools, significantly contributing to the local economy of Easton, Massachusetts. His business not only provided jobs but also supported the economy during critical periods, such as the Civil War, by supplying essential equipment.

Blacksmiths like Oliver Ames faced limited access to capital, reliance on indentured labor, and economic instability, which made success dependent on both skill and broader market conditions. They also had to manage complex operations such as labor, raw materials, shipping, and international trade while adapting from artisan craftsmanship to early industrial methods.

Oliver Ames, Senior, died in his 85th year. His one-third interest in the firms was divided among his grandsons. Frederick Lothrop Ames, Oakes Angier Ames, and Oliver Ames were taken into the partnership, while his youngest grandson, Frank Morton Ames, was later made manager of the Kingsley Iron and Machine Co. of Canton in which Oliver Ames & Sons had controlling interest. A new and larger brick office was built on the site of the previous smaller one on Main Street (torn down in 1951). On the second floor of the new building were the first two banks in Easton: the North Easton Savings Bank and the First National Bank of Easton.

Ames, Iowa was named in honor of Oakes Ames, a congressman from Massachusetts who was influential in the railroad industry. The name was proposed by railroad magnate John I. Blair, who was a friend of Ames.

full_text_zh:
老奥利弗·艾姆斯 (Oliver Ames Sr.) 是一位著名的美国铁匠和实业家，因在马萨诸塞州伊斯顿创立艾姆斯铲子工厂而闻名。他对铲子制造的贡献对该行业产生了重大影响，并帮助建立了家族财富。

奥利弗 (Oliver) 于 1817 年推出了第一台背带式铲子，提高了可用性，他的公司因生产高品质铲子而闻名，这些铲子对于横贯大陆铁路和巴拿马运河等重大建设项目至关重要。此外，1852 年一场火灾后，艾姆斯使用防火花岗岩重建了工厂，提高了生产的安全性和耐用性。

老奥利弗·艾姆斯 (Oliver Ames Sr.) 建立了艾姆斯铲子工厂 (Ames Shovel Works)，该工厂成为铲子和其他工具的主要制造商，为马萨诸塞州伊斯顿的当地经济做出了重大贡献。他的企业不仅提供就业机会，还通过提供必要的设备来支持内战等关键时期的经济。

像奥利弗·艾姆斯这样的铁匠面临着获得资本的机会有限、对契约劳工的依赖以及经济不稳定，这使得成功取决于技能和更广泛的市场条件。他们还必须管理复杂的业务，如劳动力、原材料、运输和国际贸易，同时从手工艺适应早期的工业方法。

老奥利弗·艾姆斯 (Oliver Ames) 去世，享年 85 岁。他在公司中三分之一的权益分配给了他的孙子。弗雷德里克·洛思罗普·艾姆斯 (Frederick Lothrop Ames)、奥克斯·安吉尔·艾姆斯 (Oakes Angier Ames) 和奥利弗·艾姆斯 (Oliver Ames) 加入了合伙企业，而他最小的孙子弗兰克·莫顿·艾姆斯 (Frank Morton Ames) 后来被任命为坎顿金斯利钢铁机械公司 (Kingsley Iron and Machine Co.) 的经理，奥利弗·艾姆斯父子 (Oliver Ames & Sons) 拥有该公司的控股权。在主街上先前较小的办公室（于 1951 年拆除）的旧址上建造了一间更大的新砖砌办公室。新大楼的二楼是伊斯顿最早的两家银行：北伊斯顿储蓄银行和伊斯顿第一国民银行。

爱荷华州艾姆斯的名字是为了纪念奥克斯·艾姆斯（Oakes Ames），一位来自马萨诸塞州的国会议员，他在铁路行业具有影响力。这个名字是由艾姆斯的朋友、铁路巨头约翰·布莱尔提出的。

Another straight six that deserves a mention.  This is another great six.

title_en:
Another straight six that deserves a mention.  This is another great six.

American Motors Corporation was the smallest of the major American manufacturers, and much of its history was defined by limited budgets and the need to make existing engineering go further than its competitors did. Chrysler acquired AMC in 1987, and the AMC name disappeared from new cars the following year. But one of the company's most successful creations survived long after the company itself was gone: the 4.0-litre inline-six. Introduced for the 1987 model year, the engine was not an entirely new design but a substantial development of AMC's long-running six-cylinder architecture, adapted for the increasingly demanding role of the Jeep. It displaced 242 cubic inches, or 3,965 cc, with a 3.88-inch bore and 3.41-inch stroke. The most important change was the adoption of electronic fuel injection in place of the carburetor, transforming an old-fashioned engine architecture into something much more suitable for modern vehicle use.

The difference between the two systems mattered particularly in a Jeep. A carburetor relies on airflow through a venturi to create a pressure drop that draws fuel from a float bowl. It is a mechanical arrangement that works well under ordinary conditions, but it has limitations. Cold starting requires a choke, mixture calibration can drift, and changes in altitude affect how much fuel is delivered relative to the available air. Electronic fuel injection replaces that mechanical dependence with sensors and computer-controlled metering. The system can account for coolant temperature, intake-air temperature, throttle position, and engine speed, adjusting fuel delivery as operating conditions change. For an off-road vehicle, the advantages are substantial. A carburetor can suffer fuel-delivery problems when a vehicle is climbing or descending at extreme angles, while a fuel-injected engine is far less affected by vehicle attitude. At high altitude, where thinner air would otherwise produce an excessively rich mixture, the injection system can compensate automatically. The driver can concentrate on navigating the terrain instead of managing the fuel system.

The original 4.0 produced approximately 173 horsepower and 220 lb-ft of torque in the Cherokee and Wrangler. A major revision for 1991 introduced a redesigned cylinder head and intake system, raising output to around 190 horsepower and 225 lb-ft. Those figures were not extraordinary, but the engine's strength was never its peak horsepower. Its 3.41-inch stroke and six-cylinder configuration provided useful torque at low engine speeds, exactly where a Jeep needed it when crawling over rocks, climbing steep trails, or pulling through difficult terrain. At those speeds, the ability to deliver steady torque without constantly slipping the clutch or building engine revs mattered far more than a high peak-power figure. The construction also reflected AMC's priorities. The engine retained a cast-iron block, pushrods, two valves per cylinder, and seven main bearings. It was not technologically elaborate, and much of its mechanical work could be handled without specialised equipment. Its design favoured durability, straightforward servicing, and the ability to keep working far from a dealership.

The 4.0 became the defining engine of the modern Jeep, appearing in the Cherokee, Wrangler, and Grand Cherokee across successive generations. It remained in production through the 2006 model year, giving it a lifespan of roughly two decades in vehicles that subjected it to everything from daily commuting to serious off-road use. That longevity was especially remarkable given the circumstances of its birth. AMC had developed the engine with limited resources, yet it outlasted the company that created it and continued serving under Chrysler ownership for years. It was not the most powerful six-cylinder, the most advanced, or the most sophisticated. It simply delivered the characteristics Jeep owners needed: dependable starting, useful low-speed torque, uncomplicated construction, and the ability to keep running under conditions that would expose the weaknesses of less suitable engines. AMC disappeared, but its 4.0 kept going.

full_text_zh:
另一个值得一提的直六。 这又是一个伟大的六人组。

美国汽车公司是美国主要制造商中规模最小的，其历史的大部分时间都是由有限的预算和使现有工程比竞争对手走得更远的需要决定的。克莱斯勒于 1987 年收购了 AMC，次年 AMC 名称从新车中消失。但该公司最成功的产品之一在公司消失后很长一段时间内仍然存在：4.0升直列六缸发动机。该发动机于 1987 年推出，并非全新设计，而是 AMC 长期运行的六缸架构的重大发展，适应了吉普车日益增长的需求。它的排量为 242 立方英寸，即 3,965 cc，缸径为 3.88 英寸，冲程为 3.41 英寸。最重要的变化是采用电子燃油喷射代替化油器，将老式发动机架构转变为更适合现代车辆使用的架构。

这两个系统之间的差异对于吉普车来说尤其重要。化油器依靠通过文丘里管的气流产生压降，从浮筒中吸取燃料。这是一种在普通条件下工作良好的机械装置，但它也有局限性。冷启动需要阻风门，混合物校准可能会漂移，并且海拔高度的变化会影响相对于可用空气输送的燃油量。电子燃油喷射用传感器和计算机控制的计量取代了机械依赖。该系统可以考虑冷却液温度、进气温度、节气门位置和发动机转速，并根据工况变化调整燃油输送量。对于越野车来说，优势是巨大的。当车辆以极端角度爬坡或下降时，化油器可能会遇到燃油输送问题，而燃油喷射发动机受车辆姿态的影响要小得多。在高海拔地区，空气稀薄会产生过浓的混合物，喷射系统可以自动补偿。驾驶员可以专注于驾驶地形，而不是管理燃油系统。

切诺基和牧马人的原始 4.0 发动机可产生约 173 马力和 220 磅英尺的扭矩。 1991 年的重大修改引入了重新设计的气缸盖和进气系统，将输出提高到约 190 马力和 225 磅英尺。这些数字并不特别，但发动机的强度从来都不是其峰值马力。其 3.41 英寸冲程和六缸配置在低发动机转速下提供了有用的扭矩，这正是吉普车在岩石上爬行、攀爬陡峭小径或驶过困难地形时所需要的扭矩。在这些速度下，在不不断打滑离合器或提高发动机转速的情况下提供稳定扭矩的能力比高峰值功率数字更重要。该建设也反映了 AMC 的优先事项。该发动机保留了铸铁缸体、推杆、每个气缸两个气门和七个主轴承。它在技术上并不复杂，并且其大部分机械工作无需专门设备即可完成。它的设计注重耐用性、简单的维修以及能够在远离经销商的地方继续工作。

4.0 成为现代吉普车的决定性发动机，出现在切诺基、牧马人和大切诺基历代车型中。它在 2006 车型年一直在生产，使其在车辆中的使用寿命约为二十年，可以满足从日常通勤到严重越野使用的各种需求。考虑到其诞生的环境，这种长寿尤其引人注目。 AMC 用有限的资源开发了这款发动机，但它比制造它的公司寿命更长，并继续在克莱斯勒旗下服务多年。它不是最强大、最先进或最复杂的六缸发动机。它只是提供了吉普车车主所需的特性：可靠的启动、有用的低速扭矩、简单的结构以及在暴露不太合适的发动机的弱点的条件下保持运行的能力。 AMC消失了，但它的4.0仍在继续。

消失。但该公司最成功的产品之一在公司消失后很长一段时间内仍然存在：4.0升直列六缸发动机。该发动机于 1987 年推出，并非全新设计，而是 AMC 长期运行的六缸架构的重大发展，适应了吉普车日益增长的需求。它的排量为 242 立方英寸，即 3,965 cc，缸径为 3.88 英寸，冲程为 3.41 英寸。最重要的变化是采用电子燃油喷射代替化油器，将老式发动机架构转变为更适合现代车辆使用的架构。

这两个系统之间的差异对于吉普车来说尤其重要。化油器依靠通过文丘里管的气流产生压降，从浮筒中吸取燃料。这是一种在普通条件下工作良好的机械装置，但它也有局限性。冷启动需要阻风门，混合物校准可能会漂移，并且海拔高度的变化会影响相对于可用空气输送的燃油量。电子燃油喷射用传感器和计算机控制的计量取代了机械依赖。该系统可以考虑冷却液温度、进气温度、节气门位置和发动机转速，并根据工况变化调整燃油输送量。对于越野车来说，优势是巨大的。当车辆以极端角度爬坡或下降时，化油器可能会遇到燃油输送问题，而燃油喷射发动机受车辆姿态的影响要小得多。在高海拔地区，空气稀薄会产生过浓的混合物，喷射系统可以自动补偿。驾驶员可以专注于驾驶地形，而不是管理燃油系统。

切诺基和牧马人的原始 4.0 发动机可产生约 173 马力和 220 磅英尺的扭矩。 1991 年的重大修改引入了重新设计的气缸盖和进气系统，将输出提高到约 190 马力和 225 磅英尺。这些数字并不特别，但发动机的强度从来都不是其峰值马力。其 3.41 英寸冲程和六缸配置在低发动机转速下提供了有用的扭矩，这正是吉普车在岩石上爬行、攀爬陡峭小径或驶过困难地形时所需要的扭矩。在这些速度下，在不不断打滑离合器或提高发动机转速的情况下提供稳定扭矩的能力比高峰值功率数字更重要。该建设也反映了 AMC 的优先事项。该发动机保留了铸铁缸体、推杆、每个气缸两个气门和七个主轴承。它在技术上并不复杂，并且其大部分机械工作无需专门设备即可完成。它的设计注重耐用性、简单的维修以及能够在远离经销商的地方继续工作。

4.0 成为现代吉普车的决定性发动机，出现在切诺基、牧马人和大切诺基历代车型中。它在 2006 车型年一直在生产，使其在车辆中的使用寿命约为二十年，可以满足从日常通勤到严重越野使用的各种需求。考虑到其诞生的环境，这种长寿尤其引人注目。 AMC 用有限的资源开发了这款发动机，但它比制造它的公司寿命更长，并继续在克莱斯勒旗下服务多年。它不是最强大、最先进或最复杂的六缸发动机。它只是提供了吉普车车主所需的特性：可靠的启动、有用的低速扭矩、简单的结构以及在暴露不太合适的发动机的弱点的条件下保持运行的能力。 AMC消失了，但它的4.0仍在继续。

title_en:

“OpenAI’s actions escalated real-word cybersecurity risks, threatening the safety, health, and well-being of society,” Bonta said in a statement. “The company knowingly tested a dangerous product without proper oversight or safety procedures and misled the public about it — this disregard for public safety violated California law. title_en:
🦔Customers at several of the biggest U.S. banks, including Wells Fargo and U.S. Bank, reported trouble logging in and moving money today, according to Downdetector. None of the banks has said what went wrong yet.

My Take
Microsoft’s email went dark for 13 hours on Thursday, the FAA grounded every flight on Friday, and today bank customers couldn’t reach their money. Last month AI agents broke into more than 100 companies for about $50 a pop. Each of these has its own explanation so far, and none has been pinned on AI.

Underneath all of it, companies keep cutting the people who catch problems before customers do, then bolt automation and AI onto systems that were already fragile, and the six biggest banks alone dropped about 15,000 jobs in the first quarter. I’m not anti-AI, but we’re moving faster than the plumbing can handle, and weeks like this one turn into normal until companies care as much about keeping the lights on as they do about their next AI announcement.

title_en:
AI can turn a simple description into a stunning 3D game demo but can it build something that’s actually fun, functional, and worth paying for?

That’s what caught my attention about Game Forge on @termix_ai.

The service lets you describe the game you want, and an agent takes on the build. The custom 3D game service i found starts at $200.

Now, I’d genuinely like to see how this plays out.

We’ve all come across AI-generated games that look incredible in a short clip. But looking good in a demo and being fun to play are two very different things.

What happens when someone actually pays for the service?

Does the game work? Are the controls and mechanics enjoyable? Does the agent deliver what the customer described?

Those are the questions I’m interested in.

The idea of AI agents taking on paid game development work is cool, but seeing a finished game go from a customer’s brief to a playable product would be much more convincing.

That’s the part I’ll be watching.

I think software engineering is about to develop a new kind of technical debt.

Comprehension debt.

Here's how it happe
title_en:
I think software engineering is about to develop a new kind of technical debt.

Comprehension debt.

Here's how it happens:

A developer asks an AI agent to build a feature.

The agent creates the database schema, APIs, frontend components, tests and documentation.

Everything works.

The PR is merged.

But the developer only understands 30% of what was actually changed.

Now imagine doing this for 20 features.

Eventually, you have a codebase that works, but nobody on the team has a complete mental model of it.

The scary part isn't that AI writes bad code.

It's that AI can write perfectly acceptable code faster than a team can understand it.

I think future engineering teams will need to measure not just how quickly they ship, but how much of their codebase they can still explain and maintain.

In the coming years, I believe genuine
title_en:
My greatest conviction about AI is that it will fundamentally erode work ethic.

In the coming years, I believe genuine work ethic will command a 10x premium.

We spend eight figures on service providers and interface with hundreds of employees across some of the world’s largest companies. I’ve witnessed an INSANE amount of critical judgment being outsourced to LLMs.

And it’s becoming increasingly apparent how difficult it is to find people with genuine grit, persistence, and an indefatigable desire to excel.

I see it within my own company, in new hires, across service providers, and even among our clients.

I believe the future of human capital will be defined by two axes:

1.) Work ethic: The intrinsic desire to go above and beyond, driven by personal standards of excellence, regardless of immediate recognition, compensation, or short-term outcomes.

2.) Irreplaceable skill: The possession of judgment, creativity, intuition, and specialized capabilities that are exceptionally difficult to replicate, even with increasingly sophisticated AI.

When these two qualities intersect, you have an individual who can command extraordinary amounts of capital in an AI-abundant world.

As intelligence becomes increasingly commoditized, the economic value of people who possess both exceptional ability and an insatiable desire to apply it will compound.

And I believe the gap between these individuals and everyone else will widen dramatically.

title: The current Bulgaria’s confrontation with Kaufland and Lidl is not only a dispute over food prices, inspections or compe
title_en:
The current Bulgaria’s confrontation with Kaufland and Lidl is not only a dispute over food prices, inspections or competition rules, but is also a case study in how an economic conflict can be turned into a political and information campaign.

On November 9, Bulgaria’s Commission for Protection of Competition fined Kaufland Bulgaria a record €75.7 million over alleged unfair trading practices toward Bulgarian producers and suppliers. Kaufland says it will appeal. The next day, authorities temporarily closed a Lidl store in the city of Vidin after food-safety violations were found. Lidl says it was subjected to “unprecedented institutional pressure,” noting 171 inspections in the last two weeks of October alone, against an average of 86 per month earlier in the year.

The government presents this as consumer and producer protection. That may be part of the story: large retailers do have real market power, and scrutiny of supplier relations, pricing and food safety is legitimate. But the scale, timing and political amplification of the campaign matter. When regulators, ministers, MPs, trade unions and nationalist commentators all converge on the same corporate target, the effect is no longer simply enforcement. It becomes a demonstration of political power.

This fits a familiar disinformation and influence model: identify a large, foreign-owned company; frame it as an enemy of “ordinary Bulgarians,” local producers and national sovereignty; amplify isolated violations into a story of systematic betrayal; then call for boycotts, prosecutions or expulsion. The aim is not necessarily to prove every allegation but to create a moral and emotional narrative in which the company becomes a symbol of foreign exploitation, and the state becomes its defender.

Revival's leader Kostadin Kostadinov has called publicly for a boycott of Kaufland, urged citizens to buy from “Bulgarian companies,” and asked the Prosecutor’s Office to investigate the chain. Online groups have organised a seven-day national boycott from November 16 to 22nd. A classic escalation pattern as a regulatory dispute becomes a nationalist mobilisation, and a commercial grievance becomes a question of patriotism.

There is - of course - a disinformation aspect. The narrative works by merging separate grievances into one emotionally charged story: Germany is portrayed as pressuring Bulgaria over Ukraine funding, German-owned retailers are presented as symbols of foreign economic dominance, and the government’s actions against Kaufland and Lidl are framed as a defence of Bulgarian producers, workers and consumers. This allows nationalist and pro-Kremlin actors to turn a regulatory dispute into a sovereignty issue, portraying Kaufland and Lidl not simply as companies facing inspections or fines, but as instruments of German pressure on Bulgaria. The result is a familiar disinformation pattern: a real economic conflict is amplified through anti-German and anti-foreign-capital rhetoric, boycott calls and demands for state retaliation, while the absence of public evidence linking the retailers directly to Merz’s Ukraine policy is obscured by the strength of the political narrative.

Why Kaufland and Lidl, but not Billa? The most obvious common factor is that Kaufland and Lidl belong to Germany’s Schwarz Group, while Billa is Austrian. That has led some observers to see an anti-German dimension in the campaign. It is a plausible interpretation, especially in a political environment where foreign ownership, “German influence” and national sovereignty are frequently weaponised.

A more cautious reading is that Kaufland and Lidl are the largest and most visible targets, with extensive store networks, supply chains and public exposure. Kaufland received the record competition fine; Lidl then became the focus of food-safety inspections and a highly publicised closure. Billa’s management has also said that the business environment is tense and that inspections against parts of the business are not normal. In other words, Billa may be affected by the same climate, but has not yet become the central symbol of the campaign.

The danger is that legitimate oversight gets mixed with political theatre. Bulgaria has every right to enforce competition law, food-safety rules and tax obligations. But a state campaign that treats a major investor as a nationalist enemy, encourages boycotts and blurs enforcement with propaganda risks damaging investor confidence, supply chains, jobs and Bulgaria’s reputation as a predictable place to do business.

The key question is not whether big retailers should be regulated - they should - but whether Bulgaria is enforcing clear rules through transparent institutions, or using regulation, rhetoric and nationalist mobilisation to discipline companies and mobilise political support.

full_text_zh:
当前保加利亚与考夫兰和利德尔的对抗不仅是食品价格、检查或竞争规则的争端，也是经济冲突如何转化为政治和信息运动的案例研究。

11 月 9 日，保加利亚竞争保护委员会因涉嫌对保加利亚生产商和供应商采取不公平贸易行为而对 Kaufland Bulgaria 处以创纪录的 7570 万欧元罚款。考夫兰表示将上诉。第二天，当局在发现食品安全违规行为后暂时关闭了维丁市的一家 Lidl 商店。 Lidl 表示，它受到了“前所未有的机构压力”，仅在 10 月份的最后两周就进行了 171 次检查，而今年早些时候平均每月进行 86 次检查。

政府将此视为消费者和生产者保护。这可能是故事的一部分：大型零售商确实拥有真正的市场力量，对供应商关系、定价和食品安全的审查是合法的。但竞选活动的规模、时机和政治影响力很重要。当监管者、部长、国会议员、工会和民族主义评论员齐心协力实现同一个企业目标时，其效果就不再是简单的强制执行。它成为政治权力的展示。

这符合一个熟悉的虚假信息和影响力模型：确定一家大型外资公司；将其视为“普通保加利亚人”、当地生产者和国家主权的敌人；将孤立的侵犯行为放大为系统性背叛的故事；然后呼吁抵制、起诉或驱逐。其目的不一定是证明每一项指控，而是创造一种道德和情感叙事，使该公司成为外国剥削的象征，而国家成为其捍卫者。

复兴运动的领导人科斯塔丁·科斯塔迪诺夫公开呼吁抵制考夫兰，敦促公民从“保加利亚公司”购买商品，并要求检察官办公室调查该连锁店。网络团体从11月16日至22日组织了为期7天的全国抵制活动。监管争端演变为民族主义动员，商业不满演变为爱国主义问题，这是一种经典的升级模式。

当然，还有虚假信息的一面。该叙事将不同的不满融合成一个充满情感的故事：德国被描述为就乌克兰资金问题向保加利亚施压，德国零售商被描述为外国经济主导地位的象征，政府针对考夫兰和利德尔的行动被描述为对保加利亚生产商、工人和消费者的保护。这使得民族主义者和亲克里姆林宫的行为者能够将监管争端转化为主权问题，将考夫兰和利德尔不仅描绘成面临检查或罚款的公司，而且描绘成德国向保加利亚施压的工具。其结果是一种常见的虚假信息模式：反德和反外国资本的言论、抵制呼吁和要求国家报复的言论放大了真正的经济冲突，而缺乏将零售商与梅尔茨的乌克兰政策直接联系起来的公开证据却被强大的政治叙事所掩盖。

为什么选择 Kaufland 和 Lidl，而不是 Billa？最明显的共同点是考夫兰和利德尔都属于德国施瓦茨集团，而比拉则是奥地利人。这导致一些观察家在竞选活动中看到了反德的一面。这是一个看似合理的解释，尤其是在外国所有权、“德国影响力”和国家主权经常被武器化的政治环境下。

更谨慎的解读是，Kaufland 和 Lidl 是最大、最明显的目标，拥有广泛的商店网络、供应链和公众曝光度。考夫兰收到创纪录的比赛罚款；随后，Lidl 成为食品安全检查的焦点，并被大肆关闭。比拉的管理层也表示，经营环境紧张，对部分业务的检查不正常。换句话说，比拉可能受到同样气候的影响，但尚未成为该运动的中心符号。

危险在于合法的监督与政治戏剧混在一起。保加利亚完全有权执行竞争法、食品安全规则和纳税义务。但将主要投资者视为民族主义敌人、鼓励抵制并通过宣传模糊执法的国家运动可能会损害投资者信心、供应链、就业以及保加利亚作为可预测经商之地的声誉。

关键问题不在于大型零售商是否应该受到监管——他们应该受到监管——而是保加利亚是否通过透明的机构执行明确的规则，或者利用监管、言论和民族主义动员来约束公司并动员政治支持。

lgaria 处以创纪录的 7570 万欧元罚款。考夫兰表示将上诉。第二天，当局在发现食品安全违规行为后暂时关闭了维丁市的一家 Lidl 商店。 Lidl 表示，它受到了“前所未有的机构压力”，仅在 10 月份的最后两周就进行了 171 次检查，而今年早些时候平均每月进行 86 次检查。

政府将此视为消费者和生产者保护。这可能是故事的一部分：大型零售商确实拥有真正的市场力量，对供应商关系、定价和食品安全的审查是合法的。但竞选活动的规模、时机和政治影响力很重要。当监管者、部长、国会议员、工会和民族主义评论员齐心协力实现同一个企业目标时，其效果就不再是简单的强制执行。它成为政治权力的展示。

这符合一个熟悉的虚假信息和影响力模型：确定一家大型外资公司；将其视为“普通保加利亚人”、当地生产者和国家主权的敌人；将孤立的侵犯行为放大为系统性背叛的故事；然后呼吁抵制、起诉或驱逐。其目的不一定是证明每一项指控，而是创造一种道德和情感叙事，使该公司成为外国剥削的象征，而国家成为其捍卫者。

复兴运动的领导人科斯塔丁·科斯塔迪诺夫公开呼吁抵制考夫兰，敦促公民从“保加利亚公司”购买商品，并要求检察官办公室调查该连锁店。网络团体从11月16日至22日组织了为期7天的全国抵制活动。监管争端演变为民族主义动员，商业不满演变为爱国主义问题，这是一种经典的升级模式。

当然，还有虚假信息的一面。该叙事将不同的不满融合成一个充满情感的故事：德国被描述为就乌克兰资金问题向保加利亚施压，德国零售商被描述为外国经济主导地位的象征，政府针对考夫兰和利德尔的行动被描述为对保加利亚生产商、工人和消费者的保护。这使得民族主义者和亲克里姆林宫的行为者能够将监管争端转化为主权问题，将考夫兰和利德尔不仅描绘成面临检查或罚款的公司，而且描绘成德国向保加利亚施压的工具。其结果是一种常见的虚假信息模式：反德和反外国资本的言论、抵制呼吁和要求国家报复的言论放大了真正的经济冲突，而缺乏将零售商与梅尔茨的乌克兰政策直接联系起来的公开证据却被强大的政治叙事所掩盖。

为什么选择 Kaufland 和 Lidl，而不是 Billa？最明显的共同点是考夫兰和利德尔都属于德国施瓦茨集团，而比拉则是奥地利人。这导致一些观察家在竞选活动中看到了反德的一面。这是一个看似合理的解释，尤其是在外国所有权、“德国影响力”和国家主权经常被武器化的政治环境下。

更谨慎的解读是，Kaufland 和 Lidl 是最大、最明显的目标，拥有广泛的商店网络、供应链和公众曝光度。考夫兰收到创纪录的比赛罚款；随后，Lidl 成为食品安全检查的焦点，并被大肆关闭。比拉的管理层也表示，经营环境紧张，对部分业务的检查不正常。换句话说，比拉可能受到同样气候的影响，但尚未成为该运动的中心符号。

危险在于合法的监督与政治戏剧混在一起。保加利亚完全有权执行竞争法、食品安全规则和纳税义务。但将主要投资者视为民族主义敌人、鼓励抵制并通过宣传模糊执法的国家运动可能会损害投资者信心、供应链、就业以及保加利亚作为可预测经商之地的声誉。

关键问题不在于大型零售商是否应该受到监管——他们应该受到监管——而是保加利亚是否通过透明的机构执行明确的规则，或者利用监管、言论和民族主义动员来约束公司并动员政治支持。

The open-source LLM ecosystem could really benefit from an LLM building-block API.

We have so many LLM components acros
title_en:
The open-source LLM ecosystem could really benefit from an LLM building-block API.

We have so many LLM components across different models now. Whether you are using PyTorch or C++ and CUDA code directly, there is a major switching cost when you want to run experiments or ablation studies, say swapping GQA with MLA, dense FFNs with MoE, attention layers with Mamba2 or Gated DeltaNet, or standard residual connections with attention residuals.

Currently, it’s very messy even with LLM-assisted coding.

It could maybe be on top of PyTorch or CUDA directly, but it needs to be carefully engineered and maintained (versus quickly vibe-coded on a weekend) and efficient enough that people trust it to use in production (which is really a requirement to move beyond toy examples).

Maybe some food for thought for a big, well-funded lab :)

(There are some efforts that go into that direction, like torchtitan, torchtune, Megatron Core, OLMo-core, but they are not quite that level of abstraction, I'd say. 

And, as always, there’s the chicken-and-egg problem: it needs to be popular to get widely adopted, and it needs to get widely adopted to become popular.)

• @WorkOS  – everything you need to make your app enterprise-ready. https://t.co/aiAee0oF5h

3 interesting takeaways from Satya:

1. A new form of software engineering: teams building software factories to improve their work. 

Satya cites the Azure networking team which manages 500+ fiber network operators and recently built an agentic system to better manage emails and processes. Now, they operate much more efficiently as a result. Satya sees this as the reality of “AI transformation”: brownfield work on building software factories to improve how teams operate, all while continuing the day-to-day work.

2. “Own the intelligence”: avoid lock-in & treat agents as an insider risk. 

Satya cautions companies to avoid lock-in with any single model provider by ensuring that the harness, memory, and model are not coupled, so that they can be changed with ease. He also thinks more companies should consider using open models as a way to protect their core intellectual property (IP) from leaking out, and build private evals to decide what models to use and upgrade to. He also says that models are intelligent but unreliable, so it’s best to treat them as “insider risks” and build a separate system to verify that agentic systems work as expected.

3. What’s with those voluntary exit offers? 

I asked Satya directly why Microsoft recently made voluntary exit offers to most of its software engineers for the first time in the company’s history. I also wanted to know if it could mean layoffs in the future. Unsurprisingly, his reply was diplomatic, but in the podcast I rehashed what I heard in a more direct way.

Satya 的 3 个有趣要点：

1. 一种新的软件工程形式：团队构建软件工厂来改进他们的工作。

Hockey has become a pioneer of sophisticated in-production AI deployment.  AI systems in the NHL now process data from tracking cameras, wearables, and video feeds simultaneously, producing live xG models, zone entry logs, and player load metrics that coaching staffs can act on between periods and real-time during games.

Good input data is the key to all of this, and the puck-and-player tracking system deployed league-wide captures position data at 60 frames per second from cameras embedded throughout arenas, allowing for a whole new range of advance states.

And the AHL is becoming a data laboratory, with predictive models on prospect trajectories.
